title: Usage Insights (route/model cost drivers) — working notes / open questions
content:
Context / why this doc exists
- Scratchpad for engineering decisions + gotchas while we build in-console usage insights (top cost drivers by route + model) and export reports.
- This is intentionally informal. Anything “real” should end up in Confluence ADR/specs.

Owner notes (Nadia)
- Biggest risk remains cardinality + correctness when smart routing / fallback changes models mid-request.
- Second biggest risk is customer expectations: route-level totals won’t perfectly match invoices in all timing windows (late metering + rounding + retention).


Current design intent (as of 2026-02-21)
1) Add `route` and `model` dimensions to telemetry
- Goal: allow aggregations by (org, project, env, region, deployment_mode, route, model).
- Route sources:
  a) SDK-supplied route identifier (preferred).
  b) Gateway-derived route (fallback; best-effort).
  c) If both missing/invalid => `route = "unknown"` (or "unknown_route"; need to standardize exact string in spec).

2) “Model” in insights means model variant actually used for tokens
- In smart routing scenarios: we should attribute cost to the model that generated each token segment.
- UI will likely present model breakdown as “effective model used” (NOT “requested model”) since spend follows actual work.

3) Aggregations
- Hourly + daily rollups for:
  - token counts (input/output/cached)
  - cost fields (total cost + unit cost)
  - p50/p95 latency, error rate
- Console will query hourly for short ranges and daily for longer ranges (query cost control).

4) Exports
- Export job creates bounded CSV + JSON with the same dimensions/metrics as the console views.
- Must be audit logged (who/when/filters/row count/file size).


Route dimension details (open questions + partial decisions)
Normalization rules (draft; see ADR)
- Length limit: 120 chars (confirm)
- Allowed chars: [a-zA-Z0-9._/-] + colon? (amendment: colon is useful for namespace-ish patterns, but might encourage explosion)
- Trim whitespace. Reject if contains spaces / control chars.
- No query params (strip “?…”) if gateway-derived.
- No fragments (#…)
- If SDK-supplied, do NOT attempt to parse as URL; treat as opaque string subject to allowed-char rule.

Case sensitivity
- Leaning: preserve case for SDK route (avoid surprising customers), but store an additional normalized key for grouping?
- Concern: case differences blow up cardinality (“Checkout” vs “checkout”).
- Proposal: store `route_original` only at raw event level (not in aggregates), store `route` as normalized lower-case for aggregations.
- TODO: confirm with DevEx/docs team that we can message “routes are case-insensitive”.

Cardinality guardrails (Thomas)
- Need a hard budget per (org, project) for distinct routes per day/hour.
- Proposed behavior when budget exceeded:
  - Keep top-N routes by volume/cost; roll rest into `route="__other__"`.
  - OR hash unknown routes into buckets (bad for customer comprehension).
  - OR drop route dimension for over-budget events (route=null) and show as “unattributed”.
- My preference: `__other__` bucket + a visible warning in UI.
- TBD: how to calculate “top-N” without already having the route dimension… chicken/egg. Might require streaming heavy hitters sketch (Count-Min / SpaceSaving) at ingest.

Dynamic route IDs
- Must explicitly warn against including user IDs, UUIDs, timestamps.
- We should consider “pattern recognition” to auto-detect high-entropy routes and rewrite to `__high_cardinality__` bucket.
- Open: do we want to block requests that include invalid route header? Probably not; we should accept request but ignore route and emit a warning header / console notice.


Model dimension details
Definition
- Use canonical model identifier from routing layer (e.g., “llama-3.1-70b-instruct@2026-02-10” or internal model_id).
- Needs to represent the actual variant used so cost maps cleanly.

Requested vs effective model
- We currently only plan to expose “model” in insights.
- For customers debugging routing: they may ask “I requested X but you used Y”.
- Option: add separate dimension `requested_model` later (non-goal for GA). For now, include it in raw logs only (if easy) and keep out of aggregation to avoid extra dimension blowup.

Quantization / hardware profile
- If we route to quantized variants based on load, “model” should include quantization profile if it materially changes cost.
- Open: should that be a separate dimension (`profile`) or part of `model` string?
- Strong preference: include in `model` (keeps UI simple) but makes reconciliation harder if customers expect one model name.


Edge cases / correctness notes
1) Smart routing / fallback mid-request
Scenario:
- Request starts on Model A, fails over to Model B mid-stream (capacity, error, or policy).
Questions:
- How do we attribute latency? Total latency belongs to the route, but model breakdown needs model-specific spans.
- How do we avoid double counting input tokens? Input prompt processed twice if re-run after failover.

Proposed event schema (draft)
- Emit token metering events per “attempt” (attempt_id) and include:
  - request_id, attempt_id, route, model, start_ts/end_ts
  - input_tokens, output_tokens, cached_input_tokens
  - gpu_time_ms (if available)
  - status: success|error|cancelled
- Aggregator sums cost based on successful attempt output tokens + the input tokens actually processed.
- Need a clear definition for “processed input tokens” when a request is retried:
  - Option A (truthful compute): count input tokens for every attempt that processed them.
  - Option B (customer expectation): count input tokens only once per request.
- I think we should count truthful compute (Option A) for cost attribution because we pay for it, but this can surprise customers when retries inflate costs.
- Action: add “retry/attempt” note in docs/FAQ; consider showing “retry overhead” later.

2) Streaming responses
- Ensure we still emit final metering events even if client disconnects.
- If client disconnects, output tokens may be lower; that’s fine, but route latency might be weird (server may stop early).
- Need consistent status codes for “client_cancelled”.

3) Cache attribution
- When prefix/KV cache hits, cached tokens should appear as:
  - cached_input_tokens
  - and their cost either 0 or discounted depending on our internal accounting
- Console wants to answer: “Why did my cost drop?” => cached tokens should be visible.
- Export schema must include cached tokens and cached cost fields explicitly.

4) “Unknown route” dominates
- Expect this early in beta.
- Mitigation plan:
  - prominent UI empty/education state: “Set route identifiers in SDK to unlock route-level insights”.
  - show breakdown of unknown by SDK language? (nice-to-have; probably non-goal)

5) Cross-project leakage / RBAC
- Any aggregations must be partitioned (and queried) by org_id + project_id.
- Export jobs must enforce the same filters; no “org-wide” exports unless the user has an org-wide role.
- Audit log must include project_id and filter set.

6) Data latency vs accuracy
- Near-real-time dashboard will use ingestion-time approximations; accurate cost might land later (late token metering or corrections).
- UI must label “Data may take up to X minutes to finalize” and allow “compare vs prior period” with same completeness semantics.


Console/API considerations (notes from Chloe/Jada sync)
- Pagination model: route list needs stable sort key (total_cost desc) + cursor.
- Beware “top routes” queries: expensive group-by; need pre-aggregated tables and/or cached results.
- For route detail view:
  - Top models for route (by cost) + “other models” bucket if too many.
  - Deltas vs prior period: compute with aligned windows (e.g., last 7d vs prior 7d).
- API response should include:
  - time_window_start/end
  - data_freshness watermark
  - sample_count / request_count for reliability


Export performance / guardrails
- Early benchmark notes (from internal load tests): large time ranges + low filter selectivity can time out.
- Proposed export limits (initial):
  - Max time range: 31 days (or less for hourly granularity)
  - Max rows: 200k (hard cap)
  - Max file size: 250MB
  - CSV column set fixed for v1; add schema_version column.
- Export should encourage users to export aggregated (daily) for longer ranges rather than raw hourly.


Backfill strategy
- We cannot fully backfill route/model for historical data if route wasn’t emitted.
- Plan:
  - Aggregates available “from <launch date> forward”.
  - Optional limited backfill where gateway-derived route exists in logs (but this may be noisy and not worth it).
- Need explicit messaging in UI + release notes.


Open questions / TODO list (not exhaustive)
Route
- Exact canonical strings: unknown, other, invalid — pick and lock.
- Case rules: do we enforce lower-case at ingest?
- Cardinality over-budget behavior: `__other__` vs drop vs hash; implement heavy hitters?

Model
- How to represent quantization/hardware profile (part of model string vs separate field).
- Do we need requested_model in raw events now (for later)?

Retries/fallback
- Decide compute-truth vs customer-expectation for counting input tokens across attempts.
- If we count compute-truth, do we need a separate “overhead” metric in UI later?

Latency attribution
- For multi-attempt requests, do we attribute total latency only to final attempt model or split?
- Proposal: route latency always reflects end-to-end request time; model latency breakdown is best-effort and may not sum.

Exports
- Schema versioning plan: how to add columns without breaking automation (see Slack thread on schema versioning).
- Do we support “export by model within route” as separate file or one combined dataset?

RBAC/audit
- Audit event fields: confirm what Compliance needs (filters, row_count, file_hash?).
- Retention for audit events vs export files.


Pointers / where to look next
- Telemetry plumbing: GitHub redwood/pr-15432
- Aggregates + partitions: GitHub redwood/pr-15441
- API endpoints draft: Linear ENG-8423 / ENG-8424; GitHub redwood/pr-15455 / pr-15462
- Export service: Linear ENG-8425; GitHub redwood/pr-15485
- RBAC + audit logging: Linear ENG-8428; GitHub redwood/pr-15492
- Cardinality standards: Confluence cost-attribution-cardinality-guardrails
- Route ADR: Confluence adr-route-dimension-definition-and-normalization

Appendix: example route naming conventions (draft; for docs)
- Good:
  - checkout/create
  - chat/completions
  - support-agent/summarize
  - embeddings/search-index
- Bad (dynamic identifiers):
  - user/123456789
  - org/7f3a2c1b/session
  - checkout/order/9f2c1d0e

Notes to self
- Keep pushing for clear UI copy around mismatch vs invoice; Support will get tickets otherwise.
- Don’t let export scope creep into “scheduled exports” for GA (already showing up in customer asks).
